claims.statement: The critic recorded a breach of the standing ruling on delegation of authority: c-038, marked decided by sam, kept the animals declaration sentence about legally acting on behalf of a third party verbatim, which is a legal assertion the notifier signs and therefore delegation of authority, overriding c-028's explicit instruction that the clause must not be reinstated; the critic ruled the retention a panel choice rather than a Sam ruling and said to drop the sentence.
claims.quote: builds a delegation-of-authority assertion in this phase — keeps the animals declaration sentence 'I can legally act on behalf of a third party in relation to the conditions of this declaration' verbatim. A declaration statement is a legal assertion the notifier signs, so this is delegation of authority (standing ruling 2), and it overrides c-028's explicit instruction that c-038 must not reinstate the clause.

claims.statement: The critic recorded the same breach in the agent-acting-on-behalf ruling, which said the declaration keeps the one animals third-party sentence as copy: the park itself is right but the retained copy is not, and it must align with c-028's edit saying the declaration carries no third-party authority clause.
claims.quote: same breach — 'The declaration keeps the one animals third-party sentence as copy (c-038)'; the park is right, the retained copy is not. Align with c-028's edit ('carries no third-party authority clause').

claims.statement: The critic recorded a third breach: c-034's declaration legal-limit note licensed statements asserting the notifier's standing as the professional operator or their authorised agent, which is the GDS-judge sentence c-028 rejected under the standing ruling and also pre-empts c-038 by the back door, so the standing and agent wording must be removed.
claims.quote: the declaration legal-limit note licenses statements asserting 'the notifier's standing as the professional operator or their authorised agent (c-028; NNS-UN-039)'. That is the GDS-judge sentence c-028 rejected under standing ruling 2 ... Remove the standing/agent wording.

claims.statement: The critic recorded attribution drift in four items marked decided by panel that each contain a standing-ruling-2 sub-park — c-003 parking 'Name of person making entry' as the signed-in user, c-028 parking the third-party clauses, c-033 parking the session-only listing as a user-model matter, and service-name-feedback-and-support parking the Address book and Manage account link homes — and held the item-level panel attribution defensible while each parked component should be recorded as decided by sam in the detail.
claims.quote: The item-level decidedBy 'panel' is defensible because the primary decision is the panel's, but each parked component should be recorded 'decidedBy sam (standing ruling 2)' in the detail, as c-025 does for name-of-person-making-entry and D7 does for nfr-secure-internal-login and equal-access-defra-policy-sg-fc.

claims.statement: The critic recorded for the record that attribution is otherwise correct — c-039, c-040, bulk-upload, plant-operator-registration, nfr-secure-internal-login and equal-access-defra-policy-sg-fc to sam under standing rulings 2 and 3, and reference-number-prefix, import-from-existing-documents and the three out-of-scope behaviours to the panel under ruling 1 — and that no ruling builds users, sign-in, operator registration or bulk upload.
claims.quote: Correctly attributed, for the record: conflict:c-039, conflict:c-040, behaviour:bulk-upload, behaviour:plant-operator-registration, behaviour:nfr-secure-internal-login, behaviour:equal-access-defra-policy-sg-fc (sam, rulings 2/3); behaviour:reference-number-prefix, behaviour:import-from-existing-documents, behaviour:document-uploads-out-of-scope, behaviour:outbox-and-gbnag-publishing-out-of-scope, behaviour:combined-ins-list-out-of-scope (panel under ruling 1 — no standing ruling names them). No ruling builds users, sign-in, operator registration or bulk upload.

claims.statement: The critic's summary counts the work the chair had to do: six substantive cross-docket contradictions needing a decision (the lateness model, the contact obligations and page, the Balearic sentence, the country-of-origin animals tag, the commodity-type hints, and the declaration's third-party clause), five vocabulary or convention drifts needing one answer each (the meaning of provisionalCopy, parked statuses, the derived page gate, the chrome count, and the stale cross-references), and three breaches of standing ruling 2 all on the same clause plus attribution drift in four panel-marked items.
claims.quote: Cross-docket consistency: six substantive contradictions need a decision ... Five vocabulary/convention drifts also need one answer each ... Standing rulings: three breaches of ruling 2, all the same clause ... plus attribution drift where four panel-marked items contain ruling-2 sub-parks (c-003, c-028, c-033, service-name-feedback-and-support).

claims.statement: The panel files cite standing rulings by number throughout — ruling 1 parks a policy answer nobody has or new platform capability, ruling 2 puts users, sign-in, agents, delegation and registration out of phase, ruling 3 puts bulk upload out, ruling 4 ranks the policy paper and SI above the Confluence, mural and prototype tiers, and ruling 5 keeps consistency with animals absent a plants-source reason — but neither file in this slice states rulings 1, 4 and 5 in their own words, so their wording has to be inferred from the rulings that apply them.
claims.quote: Standing rulings for the first pass (2026-09-06): users, sign-in models, agents, delegation of authority, plant-operator registration and "who notifies" are out of phase; bulk upload is out of phase.
claims.note: The README enumerates only the subjects of rulings 2 and 3; the content of rulings 1, 4 and 5 is read off their repeated use in the rationales ('standing ruling 1 parks a policy answer nobody has', 'standing ruling 4 puts phnns-policy above the Confluence tier', 'standing ruling 5' as the same-as-animals consistency anchor).

claims.statement: No file in this slice names the judges or the chair: the README says each docket had three judges and a chair, and the rulings record dissent by role only ('policy judge', 'GDS judge', 'engine judge', 'GDS service-design judge', and numbered 'Judge 2'/'Judge 3' in D7), so who sat on a docket cannot be recovered from the ledger evidence.

eight dockets, three judges and a chair each, one ruling

claims.statement: Ruling c-013 says how the commodity-type POST drops lines. It keys lines by category|genus|potatoVariety and keeps those whose category is in the new type's set, which is none whenever the type really changes. When the value is unchanged or no lines exist, the page behaves like any single-question page.

claims.note: mechanism: reconciles the commodityLines collection when commodityType changes

claims.statement: Ruling c-023 makes every display place render the reference exactly as minted, with no frontend prefix, placeholder, reformatting or pattern assertion.
